Here are the external sites and collections worth trying for **Patrick Flynn, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, circa 1870**:

---

### Ancestry (subscription required)

1. **1870 United States Federal Census**
   The same census on Ancestry is separately indexed and often has entries FamilySearch missed.
   [Search Ancestry's 1870 Census](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7163/?name=Patrick_Flynn&residence=1870_Schuylkill%2C+Pennsylvania%2C+United+States)

2. **U.S. IRS Tax Assessment Lists, 1862–1918**
   Tax rolls are a great census substitute — they capture adult men who paid taxes.
   [Search IRS Tax Lists](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1264?name=Patrick_Flynn&residence=1870_Schuylkill%2C+Pennsylvania%2C+United+States)

3. **Pennsylvania Compiled Census & Census Substitutes Index, 1772–1890**
   Aggregates many Pennsylvania census-substitute records in one index.
   [Search PA Census Index](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/3570?name=Patrick_Flynn&residence=1870_Schuylkill%2C+Pennsylvania%2C+United+States)

4. **Pennsylvania County Marriage Records, 1845–1963**
   If he married around this period, a marriage record would place him in the county.
   [Search PA Marriage Records](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61324/?name=Patrick_Flynn&residence=1870_Schuylkill%2C+Pennsylvania%2C+United+States)

5. **Pennsylvania Civil War Muster Rolls, 1860–1869**
   Many Irish immigrants in Schuylkill County served in the Civil War; muster rolls can anchor his presence.
   [Search Civil War Muster Rolls](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/9040?name=Patrick_Flynn&residence=1870_Schuylkill%2C+Pennsylvania%2C+United+States)

6. **Pennsylvania Grand Army of the Republic Membership Records, 1865–1936**
   GAR records can help locate Civil War veterans well into this period.
   [Search GAR Records](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61877/?name=Patrick_Flynn&residence=1870_Schuylkill%2C+Pennsylvania%2C+United+States)

7. **Pennsylvania, Church and Town Records, 1708–1985**
   Catholic and Protestant church registers from Schuylkill County frequently survive for this period.
   [Search Church Records](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/2451?name=Patrick_Flynn&residence=1870_Schuylkill%2C+Pennsylvania%2C+United+States)

8. **Pennsylvania War of 1812 Pensions, 1866–1879**
   A long shot, but pension files sometimes contain family information useful for this era.
   [Search PA War of 1812 Pensions](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/2394?name=Patrick_Flynn&residence=1870_Schuylkill%2C+Pennsylvania%2C+United+States)

---

### Also Worth Checking (no pre-filled link)

- **Naturalization Petitions, Eastern District of Pennsylvania, 1795–1930** (Fold3):
  http://www.fold3.com/title_117/pa_eastern/
  Irish immigrants often naturalized; naturalization papers can confirm residence and origin.

- **Naturalization Petitions, Western District of Pennsylvania, 1820–1930** (Fold3):
  http://www.fold3.com/title_119/pa_western/

- **Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania Records** (Genealogy Trails — free):
  http://genealogytrails.com/penn/schuylkill/
  Volunteer-transcribed local records that may not be indexed elsewhere.

---

**Tips for Schuylkill County specifically:** It was a major coal-mining region, heavily populated with Irish immigrants in this era. If Patrick Flynn was a miner, he may appear in company records, union records, or the Molly Maguires trial records. Church registers from St. Patrick's and other Catholic parishes are also worth pursuing if you haven't already.
